title: Empirical Evaluation of a Generate–Validate–Repair Loop for Intent→Network Configuration Using a Deterministic Reachability Validator
abstract: We measure the marginal effect of wrapping a single LLM generator (declared gpt-5-mini) with a deterministic reachability validator plus at most one automated repair (a GVR loop) on intent→device-configuration tasks. In a fully preregistered paired shared-initial design (cns-m2026-01; N=300 intents, 600 episodes), the baseline generator produced execution-validated correct configurations in 299/300 tasks (99.667%). The guarded pipeline (deterministic validator ± one repair) produced 300/300 (100.0%). Paired difference = 0.00333; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap-percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Provider-call accounting: 301 model calls (300 generator calls + 1 repair call). The preregistered target improvement (10 percentage points) was not observed due to a near-ceiling baseline. All model calls, validator traces, scoring JSON, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes to enable reproducible reanalysis.

sections.introduction:
Motivation and scope. Translating high-level operator intent into correct, safe device configurations is a core NetOps automation goal. A common operational architecture places a deterministic validator (reachability/policy checker) between a proposer (LLM) and execution, optionally adding an automated repair step. Prior work proposes generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipelines but lacks preregistered paired measurements with full execution provenance. We evaluate whether a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair increases the paired rate of execution-validated, intent-satisfying configurations vs the same generator alone for a controlled emulator-backed intent corpus.
Research question. Preregistered (cns-m2026-01): Does wrapping an LLM generator with a deterministic reachability validator and allowing at most one automated repair increase the paired rate of execution-validated, intent-satisfying configurations (primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline)?
sections.related_work: Positioning. Recent NetOps and AIOps work explores intent→configuration translation, verifier-assisted pipelines, and generate–validate–repair ideas (e.g., NetConfEval prototypes and verifier pipelines; representative verified works are cited). Our run differs by (1) preregistered paired shared-initial semantics, (2) deterministic emulator-backed validator traces per episode, and (3) archival of every model call and analysis artifact with SHA‑256 for reproducibility. We do not claim generality beyond the single-model, single-validator, closed-world emulator setting.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered as cns-m2026-01 (SHA‑256 = 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7). The design is paired, shared-initial: a single generator proposal per intent is evaluated under two conditions: baseline (no validator) and guarded (deterministic validator ± one repair). Task selection: 300 intent→configuration tasks were deterministically drawn after contamination filtering; the task manifest is archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl — SHA‑256 = 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990). Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json — SHA‑256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The execution adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1.
Validator and guarded pipeline. The deterministic reachability validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) parses generated commands, simulates their effect in a closed-world emulator snapshot, enforces task constraints (allowed_touched_fields, final-state constraints), and detects unintended reachability/policy changes. If the validator rejects, the pipeline permits at most one automated repair call (preregistered repair budget = 1). The transformation and emulator-snapshot identifiers are recorded in execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256 = b6ba6a75fa59f12f6b67e16aa5702f0fb95ba94cdb8d9b7e4d9b530c1ea76eb1).
Outcome, statistical plan, and reproducibility. Outcome per pair is binary: 1 if the generator proposal, when executed, satisfies the intent and produces no unintended reachability changes; otherwise 0. Confirmatory test: exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant pairs (prespecified). Complementary uncertainty quantification: bootstrap-percentile 95% CI for paired difference (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). All model responses, provider-call traces, validator traces, per-episode scoring JSON, and analysis logs are archived with SHA‑256 (see Artifacts and Disclosure). The registered analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' produced the reported p-value and CI; its run parameters are logged (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl — SHA‑256 = 7db06f53d650b2ffc5838b392740c75681480829e5db575e44a9a065eadb965e).
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. Planned episodes = 600 (300 intents × 2 conditions). Completed episodes = 600; failed episodes = 0. Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared-initial generator calls + 1 guarded repair call). The single repair trace is archived: execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json (SHA‑256 = 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba). Per-condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv — SHA‑256 = 55eacb88c64f29dc9c5ce1ca7079eca9b4a94b5d3a2970dae019a81a1decf73b): baseline successes = 299/300 (0.996667); guarded successes = 300/300 (1.000000).
Primary confirmatory statistics. Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv — SHA‑256 = 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55): n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired difference = 0.0033333333333332993. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0 (registered exact test; see analysis log). Bootstrap-percentile 95% CI for paired difference = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729).
Interpretation. The guarded pipeline corrected the single isolated baseline error at the cost of one additional model call. Because the baseline generator was near ceiling on this deterministic emulator corpus, the absolute measurable improvement was small and the preregistered target improvement (10 percentage points) was not achieved. The exact McNemar p = 1.0 arises from the small discordant-count configuration (n10=1,n01=0) under the prespecified exact two-sided construction; the analysis log records the exact invocation and parameters (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl — SHA‑256 cited above).
sections.discussion:
Operational implications. A deterministic validator with a small repair budget can correct isolated LLM generator mistakes with a small additional cost in model calls; in workloads where baseline generator accuracy is high, measurable aggregate benefit will be small. Larger operational gains from verifier-assisted repair are most likely when: (a) the intent distribution is noisier or adversarial; (b) validator checks a richer set of execution-safety properties; or (c) iterative multi-step repair is permitted. The single observed repair episode is fully archived (execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json — SHA‑256 cited above) to enable forensic inspection.
Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared-initial semantics isolates the net marginal effect of the gate but differs from pipelines that regenerate per condition. Construct validity: the validator operationalises safety as absence of emulator-observed unintended reachability changes in a closed-world snapshot; this is a practical but limited proxy for full production risk. External validity: single model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic/emulator-backed corpus limit generalisability; results do not imply outcomes for other LLMs, validators, real devices, or human-authored intent sets. Conclusion validity: ceiling baseline reduces power to detect large improvements; the prespecified paired test and bootstrap CI are reported transparently with provenance.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered paired experiment (N=300), a deterministic reachability validator plus at most one automated repair corrected a single isolated baseline failure; aggregate improvement was 0.00333 absolute (baseline 299/300 → guarded 300/300). The practical takeaway: verifier-assisted repair can fix isolated mistakes with low cost, but demonstrable aggregate benefit depends on baseline error rate, validator coverage, and repair budget. All execution artifacts, per-episode traces, and analysis logs are archived with SHA‑256 to enable reproducible reanalysis and extension.

figure_captions: Figure 1: Histogram of repair-iterations-to-success in the guarded condition. Observed: 299 tasks required zero repairs; 1 task required one automated repair (see execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json; SHA‑256 = 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba).

Figure 2: Failure-mode categories aggregated across the corpus (validator-detected violation, syntax/parse, execution-only emulator mismatch, specification ambiguity, other). No residual failures remained after the guarded pipeline; the single baseline-only failure was corrected by the single guarded repair (episode task-000117; per-episode artifacts cited in Results).

Figure 3: Paired binary outcomes (baseline on x-axis, guarded on y-axis). The lone discordant pair (baseline=0, guarded=1) is highlighted; per-episode artifacts and validator traces for that episode are archived (execution/responses/task-000117-*.txt and execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json; cited hashes in Results).

disclosure_statement:
Disclosure Statement — archived provenance and runtime facts

Initial master prompt immutable reference (archived): provenance/master_prompt.txt — SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.
Preregistration: cns-m2026-01 (preregistration SHA‑256 = 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7). The preregistration froze the paired shared-initial design, contamination/exclusion rules, retry policy, repair budget (≤1), confirmatory exact McNemar two-sided test, and bootstrap CI plan (10,000 resamples, seed=1729).
Declared LLM(s) and model identifier: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json — SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Provider traces and per-call cache are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/call_cache/ (full manifest indexed in execution/execution_manifest.json; representative provider-call repair trace: execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json — SHA‑256: 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba).
Orchestration and tools: adapter_family 'hosted_netops_gvr_v1' orchestrated generator→validator→(optional repair). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (v5.0); transformation and emulator-snapshot identifiers are listed in execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256 = b6ba6a75fa59f12f6b67e16aa5702f0fb95ba94cdb8d9b7e4d9b530c1ea76eb1). Execution used shared-initial semantics (single generator proposal per intent reused in both conditions) as preregistered.
Artifact archival and reproducibility: every model response, provider-call trace, validator trace, per-episode scoring JSON, and analysis output is archived with SHA‑256. Representative artifact SHAs: raw results execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 176776d1c015a652ea2d28ced2be39ffbfec9b969b72ab03e1a1193b567b6dbb), task manifest execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990), per-episode example execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080), analysis paired table analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55), analysis log analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 7db06f53d650b2ffc5838b392740c75681480829e5db575e44a9a065eadb965e). The registered analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' produced the reported McNemar p-value and bootstrap CI; its run parameters are logged in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.
Autonomy boundary and human roles. The Research Director specified the topic family and approved the master prompt pre-lock. After the autonomy lock the AI autonomously performed literature review, gap selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, artifact archiving, statistical analysis, manuscript drafting, AI-based peer review, and revision. No manual technical edits of the manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock. Pre-lock infrastructure development and rehearsals existed but were not used as empirical evidence; the reported results derive from the archived run only.
Limitations (short): ceiling baseline, single-model scope (gpt-5-mini), closed-world emulator validator proxy, single-repair budget. Full limitations and per-artifact references appear in the manuscript body.
limitations: Ceiling effect: baseline success = 299/300 reduces power to detect large preregistered improvements.
Task scope and external validity: deterministic emulator-backed intent corpus; results do not directly generalise to noisy, adversarial, or human-authored intent distributions in production.
Model scope: single declared model (gpt-5-mini); no cross-model generality claimed.
Validator construct validity: safety operationalised as absence of emulator-observed unintended reachability changes in a closed-world snapshot; production safety surfaces may be broader.
Repair budget: only a single automated repair attempt was permitted; iterative multi-call repair strategies were not evaluated in this confirmatory run.
